Run boundary — Fact: this unattended stage is intake only, the repository is stated to be empty, and no implementation is made here. Delivery and visibility — Assumption: source and tests become usable in the repository when the completed run returns its result; an isolated run's source checkout stays at its snapshot until that return. No deployed target is named; any deployed outcome would exist only after release. Interaction and state — Assumption: this is a local command, with process-local state and no requested identity, shared state, persistence, or access-control system; Q5 records what that rules out. Discovery leads — Unverified leads are the eventual checkout, execution environment, project configuration, representative sales CSVs, and any format documentation; no team, channel, internal site, private repository, owner, or sensitive locator was supplied. Authority — The request grants repository delivery for the named tool and tests; it names no external target. Risk — A real sales-file schema or revenue convention may differ from the defaults, so discovery should look for evidence before those assumptions are treated as compatibility guarantees."
